findings.subject: alert
findings.summary: Alert success and warning action labels fail text contrast (3.58:1 and 3.28:1), and every Alert is an assertive role=alert with no announced tone.
findings.evidence: Measured from apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/ui-react-alert-action-variants-chromium-linux.png (darkest glyph vs fill): success 3.58:1, warning 3.28:1, need 4.5:1. alert.css:164 and :179 set --alert-action-foreground to --a63-status-success / --a63-status-warning; alert.tsx:26 hard-codes role="alert"; tone only in data-variant.
findings.fix: Use text-role tokens for the action foreground (as error does with --a63-text-danger; add --a63-text-success/-warning if missing) and declare those pairs in the contrast test. Default role to status (or none) for persistent alerts with role="alert" opt-in, and add a visually hidden tone prefix so the tone is announced.

verified.reason: alert.css:164 and :179 set --alert-action-foreground to --a63-status-success / --a63-status-warning, which are color-success-600 rgb(0,147,88) and color-warning-600 rgb(194,117,0) (primitives.css:261,272). Computed against the 4% tinted fill, that gives 3.77:1 and 3.43:1, short of the 4.5:1 needed for action label text. semantics.css:229-230 says these status tokens are tuned for 3:1 graphics, and text is meant to use the *-subtle-foreground steps (error already uses --a63-text-danger at :134). The role part is weaker than reported: alert.tsx:26 does hard-code role=alert, but {...props} comes after it, so a consumer can override it. That half is a P2 default-semantics gap. The contrast failure alone holds P1.

findings.subject: empty
findings.summary: Empty's 'Show details' toggle text is about 2.5:1 against the surface.
findings.evidence: empty.css:116 color: color-mix(in oklch, var(--a63-text-secondary) 60%, transparent); apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/ui-react-empty-error-state-chromium-linux.png darkest glyph rgb(160,160,160) on rgb(250,250,250) = 2.51:1 (12px text, needs 4.5:1). axe passes, likely because it cannot resolve color-mix alpha.
findings.fix: Draw the toggle at --a63-text-secondary (full strength) or use the muted ghost Button tone, and add a contrast assertion for it.

verified.reason: empty.css:116 sets color-mix(--a63-text-secondary 60%, transparent). --a63-text-secondary is surface-light-11 = rgb(100,100,100) (primitives.css:121), so on a page of about rgb(250,250,250) it composites to about rgb(160,160,160). That is 2.51:1, computed again here. The text is 12px (control-font-size-xs) at rest, and only :hover restores full secondary colour (empty.css:119-121). This is a WCAG 1.4.3 failure on an interactive label.

findings.subject: feedback-state
findings.summary: FeedbackState spreads no props and forwards no ref, so consumers cannot set id, aria-*, data-* or style.
findings.evidence: feedback-state.tsx:155-166 destructures a closed list; the root div (lines 173-181) gets no rest props or ref. Title/description are string-only.
findings.fix: Accept React.ComponentProps<'div'> minus the owned keys, spread the rest onto the root (React 19 passes ref), and allow ReactNode for title and description.

verified.reason: Real: FeedbackStateProps (feedback-state.tsx:49-60) is a closed interface, the destructure at :155-166 has no rest, and the root div at :173-181 takes no spread props and no ref. K1's hard requirements, however, are 'props match the contract' and 'composition spreads props/forwards refs'. The generated contract (feedback-state-contract.ts) defines only kinds, sizes, slots and states, all of which are honoured, and FeedbackState is not an asChild/render part. Consumers can still wrap it to add id or aria. This matches the bar's P2 wording ('works, with a known gap a consumer can hit'), not a ready-blocker.

findings.subject: feedback-state
findings.summary: FeedbackState's loading live region is aria-busy, and the result states drop the live region, so loading and its outcome go unannounced; the title is not a heading.
findings.evidence: feedback-state.tsx:174-180: aria-busy=true on the role=status region while loading; role/aria-live become undefined for empty, no-results, not-found, offline and stale. Title is a plain div (lines 189-191) while EmptyTitle is role=heading (empty.tsx:53-58). The test at feedback-state.test.tsx:23-32 asserts this pattern.
findings.fix: Keep one persistent polite status region that always exists, drop aria-busy from it (put aria-busy on the content region the consumer is loading if anything), keep role=alert only for error, and render the title as a heading (configurable level).

verified.reason: feedback-state.tsx:174-180 puts aria-busy=true on the role=status/aria-live=polite region while loading. Busy regions have their announcements suppressed, so 'Loading…' is not read. For empty, not-found, no-results, offline and stale, role and aria-live become undefined in the same render that swaps the text, so the region is no longer live when the outcome arrives and nothing is announced. The test at feedback-state.test.tsx:23-32 checks that this pattern is present. It does not check that anything gets announced. The title at :189-191 is a plain div, while EmptyTitle is role=heading aria-level=3 (empty.tsx:53-58). The non-heading title is minor; the missing announcements are a real K2 gap.

findings.subject: load-more-trigger
findings.summary: The Retry action is a bare text button about 15px tall with no coarse-pointer target expansion.
findings.evidence: load-more-trigger.css:88-96 (padding: 0; border: 0; inline text); glyphs span y 36-51 in apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/ui-react-loadmoretrigger-failed-chromium-linux.png; no --a63-control-min-target rule. Runtime craft passes it only through the WCAG 2.5.8 spacing exception (apps/storybook/craft/rules.ts:299-301).
findings.fix: Render Retry with the DS Button (size sm, ghost or link variant), which carries min-target handling and hover/active states, or add a ::after hit area sized to --a63-control-min-target.

verified.reason: load-more-trigger.css:88-96 gives .a63-LoadMoreTrigger-action padding 0, border 0 and inline text, with no min-height/min-width and no --a63-control-min-target. grep finds no coarse-pointer rule in that file. The design system does define --a63-control-min-target as 2.75rem under (pointer: coarse) (styles/src/contracts/environment.css:128-133), and checkbox, radio, slider, tabs and segmented-control consume it. Retry ignores it. K5 explicitly requires 44px targets on coarse pointers. The craft rule only passes it through the 24px spacing exception (rules.ts passesSpacing), which is not the 44px coarse bar.

findings.fix: Add an active treatment and a focus-visible capture.

findings.subject: badge
findings.summary: Badge heights are fixed rem and do not follow compact density.
findings.evidence: badge.css:10, sizes block: 1rem / 1.25rem / 1.5rem.
findings.fix: Derive heights from --a63-space-unit or control size tokens.

findings.subject: skeleton
findings.summary: Skeleton disappears in forced-colors mode.
findings.evidence: skeleton.css:7-12 background-color only; no @media (forced-colors: active) rule.
findings.fix: Add a forced-colors rule (for example a CanvasText 1px outline or GrayText background with forced-color-adjust: none).

findings.subject: animated-check
findings.summary: AnimatedCheck's draw duration is a raw 300ms, not a motion token.
findings.evidence: animated-check.tsx:17 animation: a63-animated-check-draw 300ms ease-out forwards.
findings.fix: Use a --a63-motion-* duration and easing token.

findings.subject: empty
findings.summary: The expanded error detail has no visual baseline.
findings.evidence: Baselines: ui-react-empty-error-state shows collapsed only.
findings.fix: Add an expanded ErrorState story.

findings.subject: alert
findings.summary: Component guidance is generic boilerplate across the batch.
findings.evidence: `pnpm -s atom63 component alert` guidance bullets 2-3 ('Keep product data and fetching outside...', 'Test long, empty, and narrow content...') repeat verbatim for badge and others.
findings.fix: Write component-specific guidance (when to use Alert vs Toaster vs FeedbackState, role choice).
